app_engine_apis.description: Allows App Engine second generation runtimes to access the legacy bundled services.
app_engine_apis.rationale: Toggles access to the legacy bundled App Engine APIs for the runtime. This is a runtime-compatibility choice rather than a structural security control, and a generic platform policy mandating it would not meaningfully harden the resource.

delete_service_on_destroy.description: If set to 'true', the service will be deleted if it is the last version.
delete_service_on_destroy.rationale: When true, destroying a version also deletes the entire parent service and all its versions. A policy should keep this disabled to prevent destructive, accidental loss of the whole service — matching the prevent-destructive-loss archetype (like force_destroy).

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

env_variables.description: Environment variables available to the application.
env_variables.rationale: Free-form key/value environment variables passed to the running version. A generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain arbitrary application-defined values, so it is not a policy target (teams should keep secrets in Secret Manager instead).

inbound_services.description: A list of the types of messages that this application is able to receive. Possible values: ["INBOUND_SERVICE_MAIL", "INBOUND_SERVICE_MAIL_BOUNCE", "INBOUND_SERVICE_XMPP_ERROR", "INBOUND_SERVICE_XMPP_MESSAGE", "INBOUND_SERVICE_XMPP_SUBSCRIBE", "INBOUND_SERVICE_XMPP_PRESENCE", "INBOUND_SERVICE_CHANNEL_PRESENCE", "INBOUND_SERVICE_WARMUP"]
inbound_services.rationale: Enables legacy App Engine bundled inbound services (e.g. mail, warmup). These are optional legacy integrations rather than a primary access control; ingress/firewall settings govern exposure, so a generic policy on this list adds no meaningful hardening.

instance_class.description:
Instance class that is used to run this version. Valid values are
AutomaticScaling: F1, F2, F4, F4_1G
BasicScaling or ManualScaling: B1, B2, B4, B4_1G, B8
Defaults to F1 for AutomaticScaling and B2 for ManualScaling and BasicScaling. If no scaling is specified, AutomaticScaling is chosen.
instance_class.rationale: Selects the CPU/memory sizing tier (e.g. F1/B1) for the version. This is a capacity/cost choice, not a security control, and no generic secure value can be enforced.

noop_on_destroy.description: If set to 'true', the application version will not be deleted.
noop_on_destroy.rationale: To ensure Terraform can fully decommission the application version.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: To automatically inherit the provider-level project ID.

runtime.rationale: Selects the language runtime/version the version executes on. A policy should whitelist currently-supported (non-deprecated, patched) runtimes so the app is not running on an end-of-life runtime with known vulnerabilities.

runtime_api_version.description:
The version of the API in the given runtime environment.
Please see the app.yaml reference for valid values at 'https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/<language>/config/appref'\
Substitute '<language>' with 'python', 'java', 'php', 'ruby', 'go' or 'nodejs'.
runtime_api_version.rationale: The application utilises a second-generation runtime where the API version is automatically managed by the platform, ensuring the environment always uses the most compatible interface without manual intervention.

service.rationale: The App Engine service name this version belongs to. This is an identifier; we do not constrain resource names.

service_account.description: The identity that the deployed version will run as. Admin API will use the App Engine Appspot service account as default if this field is neither provided in app.yaml file nor through CLI flag.
service_account.rationale: Specifies the runtime identity (service account email) the version runs as. This is a reference to a team-chosen identity; a platform policy cannot pin a specific service account, so it is not a generic policy target (IAM bindings on that account are the control).

threadsafe.description: Whether multiple requests can be dispatched to this version at once.
threadsafe.rationale: Environment to use its default concurrency settings, ensuring the application remains stable and avoids race conditions if the codebase is not optimized for parallel request handling.

version_id.description: Relative name of the version within the service. For example, 'v1'. Version names can contain only lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens. Reserved names,"default", "latest", and any name with the prefix "ah-".
version_id.rationale: To automatically generate unique timestamp identifiers for each deployment, inturn preventing naming conflicts and ensuring that new releases do not accidentally overwrite existing versions.

automatic_scaling.description: Automatic scaling is based on request rate, response latencies, and other application metrics.

automatic_scaling.max_concurrent_request.description:
Number of concurrent requests an automatic scaling instance can accept before the scheduler spawns a new instance.

Defaults to a runtime-specific value.

automatic_scaling.max_idle_instances.description: Maximum number of idle instances that should be maintained for this version.

automatic_scaling.max_pending_latency.description:
Maximum amount of time that a request should wait in the pending queue before starting a new instance to handle it.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".

automatic_scaling.min_idle_instances.description: Minimum number of idle instances that should be maintained for this version. Only applicable for the default version of a service.

automatic_scaling.min_pending_latency.description:
Minimum amount of time a request should wait in the pending queue before starting a new instance to handle it.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".

automatic_scaling.standard_scheduler_set.description:
Maximum number of instances to run for this version. Set to zero to disable maxInstances configuration.

**Note:** Starting from March 2025, App Engine sets the maxInstances default for standard environment deployments to 20. This change doesn't impact existing apps. To override the default, specify a new value between 0 and 2147483647, and deploy a new version or redeploy over an existing version. To disable the maxInstances default configuration setting, specify the maximum permitted value 2147483647.
Minimum number of instances to run for this version. Set to zero to disable minInstances configuration.
Target CPU utilization ratio to maintain when scaling. Should be a value in the range [0.50, 0.95], zero, or a negative value.
Target throughput utilization ratio to maintain when scaling. Should be a value in the range [0.50, 0.95], zero, or a negative value.

basic_scaling.description: Basic scaling creates instances when your application receives requests. Each instance will be shut down when the application becomes idle. Basic scaling is ideal for work that is intermittent or driven by user activity.

basic_scaling.idle_timeout.description:
Duration of time after the last request that an instance must wait before the instance is shut down.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s". Defaults to 900s.

basic_scaling.max_instances.description: Maximum number of instances to create for this version. Must be in the range [1.0, 200.0].

deployment.description: Code and application artifacts that make up this version.

deployment.files.description:
Manifest of the files stored in Google Cloud Storage that are included as part of this version.
All files must be readable using the credentials supplied with this call.

entrypoint.shell.description: The format should be a shell command that can be fed to bash -c.
entrypoint.shell.rationale: A free-form shell command (fed to bash -c) used as the version entrypoint. This is arbitrary application startup logic; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain an arbitrary command, so it is not a policy target.

handlers.description:
An ordered list of URL-matching patterns that should be applied to incoming requests.
The first matching URL handles the request and other request handlers are not attempted.

handlers.auth_fail_action.description: Actions to take when the user is not logged in. Possible values: ["AUTH_FAIL_ACTION_REDIRECT", "AUTH_FAIL_ACTION_UNAUTHORIZED"]

handlers.login.description: Methods to restrict access to a URL based on login status. Possible values: ["LOGIN_OPTIONAL", "LOGIN_ADMIN", "LOGIN_REQUIRED"]

handlers.redirect_http_response_code.description: 30x code to use when performing redirects for the secure field. Possible values: ["REDIRECT_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_301", "REDIRECT_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_302", "REDIRECT_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_303", "REDIRECT_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_307"]

handlers.security_level.description: Security (HTTPS) enforcement for this URL. Possible values: ["SECURE_DEFAULT", "SECURE_NEVER", "SECURE_OPTIONAL", "SECURE_ALWAYS"]

handlers.url_regex.description:
URL prefix. Uses regular expression syntax, which means regexp special characters must be escaped, but should not contain groupings.
All URLs that begin with this prefix are handled by this handler, using the portion of the URL after the prefix as part of the file path.

handlers.script.description:
Executes a script to handle the requests that match this URL pattern.
Only the auto value is supported for Node.js in the App Engine standard environment, for example "script:" "auto".

handlers.script.script_path.description: Path to the script from the application root directory.

handlers.static_files.description: Files served directly to the user for a given URL, such as images, CSS stylesheets, or JavaScript source files. Static file handlers describe which files in the application directory are static files, and which URLs serve them.

handlers.static_files.application_readab.description:
Whether files should also be uploaded as code data. By default, files declared in static file handlers are uploaded as
static data and are only served to end users; they cannot be read by the application. If enabled, uploads are charged
against both your code and static data storage resource quotas.

handlers.static_files.expiration.description:
Time a static file served by this handler should be cached by web proxies and browsers.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example "3.5s".

handlers.static_files.http_headers.description:
HTTP headers to use for all responses from these URLs.
An object containing a list of "key:value" value pairs.".

handlers.static_files.mime_type.description:
MIME type used to serve all files served by this handler.
Defaults to file-specific MIME types, which are derived from each file's filename extension.

handlers.static_files.path.description: Path to the static files matched by the URL pattern, from the application root directory. The path can refer to text matched in groupings in the URL pattern.

handlers.static_files.require_matching_f.description: Whether this handler should match the request if the file referenced by the handler does not exist.

handlers.static_files.upload_path_regex.description: Regular expression that matches the file paths for all files that should be referenced by this handler.

libraries.description: Configuration for third-party Python runtime libraries that are required by the application.

libraries.version.description: Version of the library to select, or "latest".

manual_scaling.description: A service with manual scaling runs continuously, allowing you to perform complex initialization and rely on the state of its memory over time.

manual_scaling.instances.description:
Number of instances to assign to the service at the start.

**Note:** When managing the number of instances at runtime through the App Engine Admin API or the (now deprecated) Python 2
Modules API set_num_instances() you must use 'lifecycle.ignore_changes = ["manual_scaling"[0].instances]' to prevent drift detection.

vpc_access_connector.description: Enables VPC connectivity for standard apps.

vpc_access_connector.egress_setting.description: The egress setting for the connector, controlling what traffic is diverted through it.

vpc_access_connector.name.description: Full Serverless VPC Access Connector name e.g. /projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/connectors/c1.
